issues.title: scripts/test_parallel.sh's sibling partitions trigger ISS-0110's concurrent-invocation guard inside Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest, causing reclaimed/skipped assertions to always see 0
issues.description: TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2's ISS-0110 fix defers its entire sweep whenever pg_stat_activity shows ANY other letflow_mixtest_%-tagged connection (by design, since it cannot distinguish a live sibling's row from a dead one). scripts/test_parallel.sh's own N parallel `mix test` OS processes are exactly such siblings from each other's point of view, so whichever partition runs test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs sees the other partitions as 'another invocation' and the guard defers entirely, making reclaimed/skipped always 0 regardless of what that test's own fixture set up. Reproduced directly: the 3 failing tests pass 6/6 when test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs is run alone (no sibling mix test process), and fail identically (reclaimed/skipped >= 1 asserted, got 0) inside the 4-way TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 run, with the guard's own deferral log line printed at each failure point. Not this branch's defect -- neither the test file nor tenant_schema_reaper.ex is in this branch's diff. Searched docs/issues/*.yaml and docs/anti-patterns.md first; ISS-0194/ISS-0212 cover a different test_parallel.sh defect (connection-pool exhaustion at ecto.create, already resolved) and ISS-0110 covers the original nested-invocation scenario the guard was built for, not this sibling-partition trigger of the same guard. Affected files: test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs, test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex, scripts/test_parallel.sh.
issues.evidence: test/reports/report-20260821-WF02-REQ067-20260821.yaml's failures/evidence section; isolated re-run mix test test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs -> 6 passed, 0 failed.
